rules.statement: Every spec-coverage catalog entry must carry its authoritative reference (RFC or OIDC section), its exercise channel (browser, probe-runner, or external-suite), and its tracking issue number when one is known.
rules.why: The catalog is the single source of truth for the published spec surface. The channel field makes the browser's limits visible and gives the probe runner a seam to plug into without changing the model.
rules.check: Look for new or changed catalog rows that lack a reference or a channel tag, or that are tagged browser when the feature needs a client secret, a client certificate, or a server-to-server call.

rules.statement: Keep the coverage classifier a pure, UI-free function of the discovery document, and cover each status it can return (implemented, partial, missing, non-conformant) with unit tests.
rules.why: The matrix also detects regressions, so a status change has to be a real signal rather than noise.
rules.check: Look for classifier changes that bring in UI code, network calls, or other state besides the discovery document, or that ship without matching unit tests.

rules.statement: Add support for a newly published spec as a catalog row plus a classifier, not as special-case code in the UI or a hardcoded gap list in the docs.
rules.why: A static list drifts away from the running OP. A computed, catalog-driven matrix stays accurate and shows newly implemented capabilities automatically.
rules.check: Look for hardcoded feature or gap lists in UI components or docs that duplicate catalog data.

rules.statement: The conformance probe runner CLI must exit with a non-zero code when any probe ends in the failed status.
rules.why: This lets the runner act as a CI pre-flight check.
rules.check: Look for runner changes that swallow failed probes or always exit with code 0.
